reviews.text: I would not recommend using this pet hotel. It was good that they contacted me when my pet suddenly became ill, but they didn't report the test results or share any updates on my pet's condition unless I specifically asked them. Other pet hotels provide reports on meals, bowel movements, and walks, and I was aware that this hotel didn't offer those services, but there was absolutely no communication even after my pet became ill. I think they should just close down their pet hotel business. I deeply regret leaving my pet there, so I'm reluctant to write this review, but I'm sharing it so that others don't have the same experience.

The medicine I was given had absolutely no effect.
After undergoing all the necessary tests and continuing to visit the clinic, they lashed out at me, accusing me of neglecting my pet.
Of course I didn't neglect it!
When I had my pet examined at another hospital, the diagnosis and treatment were completely different.
My pet's condition, which had worsened, recovered completely in two weeks—faster than the six months I had been going there.
I do not recommend this hospital.
First of all, the medicine is much more expensive than elsewhere. Why?
And most importantly! The waiting room smells awful.
I should have realized something was wrong when the hospital reception smelled bad.

My beloved dog was diagnosed with a rare blood disorder. Our local veterinary clinic couldn't treat it, so we brought him here because the head veterinarian is said to be an expert in blood disorders. Not only is he knowledgeable, but his care is also very attentive. Thanks to him, my dog ​​is now in remission, and we are continuing to monitor him.

I am extremely grateful.

It's extremely expensive, and they'll perform unnecessary blood tests whenever the cat becomes even slightly unwell. Because they required daily, expensive blood tests, I pointed out that "if the cat is anemic, perhaps this test isn't necessary," and the price was suddenly reduced by about half. My cat's appetite was decreasing, so I asked for instructions on how to use a syringe orally, but they strongly recommended inserting a tube into his nose. I agreed, but when I returned from the examination room, a tight cloth was wrapped around his neck to prevent the tube from coming out. The smell, which seemed to be soaked in a very strong chemical, made me feel sick, and sure enough, he collapsed. I called the hospital and told the director that he was collapsed, and they said, "I guess it was time. Shall we euthanize him?" I was heartbroken. He was walking energetically and eating a little until the day before the tube was inserted. I truly regret having brought him to this hospital, as he was such a lovely cat until the very end.

I can trust the teachers, but the receptionists and teachers are too loud... 
My child is very scared, and I think the other children are frightened as well... I think they should be a little quieter... 
It's really stressful, so I'm giving it 3 stars...

Our five Chihuahuas were treated at this hospital in the past.

One of them, when he was just one year old, was diagnosed at this hospital with a future heart condition. We later moved to Hokkaido, so we now go to a veterinary hospital there, but I now truly understand how amazing the doctors at Ueno no Mori Animal Hospital are. The dog that was predicted to have a heart condition is now 12 years old and receiving treatment for it. We've been to many veterinary hospitals since moving to Hokkaido, but no other doctor was able to predict that he would develop a heart condition.
He is a kind and patient doctor who listens to my concerns. I was deeply touched by his kindness when I had to say goodbye to my beloved dog, and I am truly grateful.
He is a very kind and caring teacher and I highly recommend him.

I'm writing this with overwhelming gratitude ❤︎
Here, a female cardiologist specializing in cardiology performed surgery on my beloved dog for mitral valve insufficiency, and a male veterinarian performed a spaying surgery afterward ☺︎

My rescued Chihuahua, who was 5 years old at the time of the surgery, had mitral valve insufficiency since being rescued, and was extremely timid, so I was extra careful when choosing a hospital for heart surgery. I was looking for a hospital with trustworthy veterinarians and a less impersonal atmosphere than large hospitals, and that's when I found an article about Ueno no Mori Animal Hospital. I had read several articles about the female veterinarian, and she is a very charming doctor who exudes passion and warmth beneath her cool demeanor ❤︎

I was incredibly anxious until the day of the surgery, but the explanations leading up to the surgery were thorough and easy to understand, and on the day of the surgery, the nurses welcomed us so kindly that I remember feeling a sense of relief. When I visited immediately after the surgery, I was deeply moved by how diligently the doctors were caring for my dog!


Currently, my dog ​​has completed her 18-month post-surgery check-up, which showed no abnormalities. During that time, she also had her fluid-filled uterus removed, and now, at 7 years old, she's like a completely different dog, full of energy and running around every day.

I've truly realized how much difference there is between animal hospitals. About two years ago, I lost my previous dog to a disease that didn't need to be treated, and afterwards, I adopted this rescue dog who looks just like her. I wish I had known about this hospital sooner. I'm filled with gratitude ❤︎ I always wish it were a little closer to my home...☺︎❤︎
